title: The best .io games to play right now
excerpt: Arena games live and die by their player count. Here are the ones still filling rooms in November, and how to tell a live server from a dead one before you commit a round.
body:
A .io game is the shortest path from a link to actual play. No install, no account, no launcher — the page loads and within a couple of seconds you are moving around an arena with everyone else who opened it at the same time.

The catch is that arena games live and die by their player count. A title that was packed last spring can sit at eleven players today, and an empty room makes even a good game feel broken. So we re-check the rooms instead of trusting last year's rankings.

## Our pick right now: Slime IO 2

[Slime IO 2](/game/slime-io-2) is the one we keep coming back to. The loop is simple enough to understand in one round — eat what is smaller than you, avoid what is bigger — and the map gives you enough room to make a mistake and recover from it.

What separates it from the dozens of clones is the pacing. Growth is fast in the first ninety seconds, so you are never stuck as a tiny blob for long. That matters more than any feature list: a .io game that takes four minutes to become interesting has already lost most of its players.

## If you want a fight instead of a grind

[Robot Battle X](/game/robot-battle-x) leans harder on combat. Rounds are shorter, respawns are faster, and the arena is small enough that you will meet someone within ten seconds. It is a worse choice if you want a relaxed session, and a better one if you have five minutes and want something to happen.

## How to tell if a server is alive

Three things to check before you invest a round:

- **Player count on the lobby screen.** Under about twenty and you will spend more time looking for opponents than fighting them.
- **Server age.** Most .io games spin up a fresh room every few hours. The newest room fills first; older rooms empty out quietly.
- **Join timing.** Rooms that opened in the last ten minutes still have players joining. Rooms that opened six hours ago usually have a handful of veterans and nobody else.

## What we skip

We drop a .io title when it stops loading reliably, when the room sits empty across several checks, or when the build has not been touched in over a year. Keeping a dead link in a list is worse than having a shorter list — the visitor clicks, waits, and leaves without playing anything.

That is also why this page changes more often than the rest of the site. Check back in a month and at least one entry here will be different.
author: WangNan

title: New browser games this week
excerpt: Eleven additions this week, from a miner that keeps pulling you back to a racing game that runs on a school laptop. Here is what went live and why it made the cut.
body:
Every week we add a batch of games and quietly drop a few that stopped working. This is the short version of what changed, so you can see the reasoning instead of just a grid of new thumbnails.

## What went live

The batch leans toward games you can pick up in a spare five minutes. That is deliberate — the majority of people opening this site are between two things, not planning a session.

- [Miner Tycoon](/game/miner-tycoon) — dig, sell, upgrade, repeat. The progression curve is steep enough that the first upgrade lands inside two minutes.
- [Cookie Kingdom](/game/cookie-kingdom) — a clicker with an actual visual payoff. Buildings appear on screen as you buy them, which makes the numbers feel less abstract.
- [Pocket Racer](/game/pocket-racer) — top-down racing that runs fine on integrated graphics. No 3D, no loading bar, no fan noise.
- [Tower Tactics](/game/tower-tactics) — a small tower defence with three maps. Short, but it respects your time and does not pad the difficulty by making waves longer.

## What we removed

Two idle games came out of the list this week. Both still loaded, but their save system broke with a browser update, which means progress vanished on refresh. A broken save is worse than a missing game: people lose an hour and blame the site.

## Why these and not the other forty

We looked at roughly forty candidates this week. Most were filtered out before they reached a page:

- **Too heavy to load.** Anything that takes more than a few seconds on a normal connection is out, regardless of quality.
- **No clean embed.** If a publisher only offers a page wrapper instead of a direct iframe, we skip it rather than work around it.
- **Duplicate of something already here.** A second farming clicker only makes sense if it does something the first one does not.

## Next week

We are testing a batch of two-player games aimed at the same-keyboard setup — the kind you play with someone sitting next to you. If the controls map cleanly on a laptop keyboard, a few of them will land next week. If they need a gamepad, they will not.

If you have played something that belongs here, send it through the contact page. We read everything, even when we cannot add it.
author: WangNan

title: How we choose the games we list
excerpt: We do not make games, so the only thing we can be trusted for is curation. Here is the exact checklist every title passes before it gets a page, and what gets it removed.
body:
We do not develop games and we do not host game files. Every title on this site runs on its publisher's own infrastructure. That means the only thing we can genuinely be trusted for is curation — deciding what is worth your click and what is not.

So here is the actual checklist, not a marketing version of it.

## What a game has to pass to get listed

1. **It loads inside a browser tab.** No download prompt, no launcher, no installer. If a game needs a desktop client, it is not a browser game.
2. **It plays on integrated graphics.** We check on a laptop without a discrete GPU, because that is what most visitors are using. A game that needs a graphics card is a game most people cannot play.
3. **The embed is first-party.** The publisher has to offer a direct iframe. We do not wrap someone else's page or strip a competitor's branding to make a game fit.
4. **Controls work on a normal keyboard.** Arrow keys and WASD, mouse for aiming, space for action. Anything that silently requires a controller gets skipped.
5. **It saves properly, or does not pretend to.** Progress that vanishes on refresh is worse than no progress at all.

## What gets a game removed

Lists rot. A page that stays up after the game behind it dies is worse than a short list, because the visitor pays the cost — they click, wait, and leave.

We remove a title when:

- it stops loading across several checks;
- the room sits empty for more than a week (multiplayer only);
- the build has not been updated in over a year and has visible breakage;
- the publisher pulls the embed or changes the terms.

## What we do not do

We do not re-host files, we do not clone another site's catalogue, and we do not put a game on a page that only exists to hold ads. Every page carries a real description, controls, and links to similar titles, because a page with nothing but an iframe is not something search engines or visitors should reward.

## How the site makes money

Advertising. Some listings may also be part of a distribution partner's revenue-share programme, which pays the site when a game is played. That does not change what gets listed — a game that fails the checklist above does not get a page because it pays better.

If you think we got a call wrong, or a game here is broken for you, the contact page goes straight to us.
author: WangNan

title: Leonida: the GTA 6 PC recompilation project, explained
excerpt: Leonida is an early static-recompilation project for the Xbox build of GTA 6. It does not boot yet, contains no game files, and is not an official Rockstar PC port.
body:
## What Leonida is

Leonida is a GitHub project that aims to run the Xbox Series version of *Grand Theft Auto VI* natively on Windows. It is a **static recompilation** project, not an emulator: the Xbox CPU is x86-64, so the game's code can be loaded and run natively while the console system software is reimplemented. Its shader pipeline translates the console's RDNA2 GPU programs to SPIR-V for Vulkan, and the game's models, textures and audio are read from a copy the user already owns.

The repository is explicit about its boundaries: it does not contain the game, keys or an executable, and it does not explain how to obtain them. The project says nothing in it decrypts or works around package protection.

## What works today

According to the project's own status table, checked on November 23, 2026:

- The repository can find and check a supported Xbox Series copy (version 1.0.2.1).
- All 26,503 shaders have been carved, unpacked and translated to SPIR-V, and the project reports that all of them passed `spirv-val` validation.
- Models, texture dictionaries and audio banks have been exported with the project's tools.
- The PE loader and import shims can run a stand-in executable end to end.
- The Xbox D3D12 to Vulkan layer is still in progress.

What does **not** work: booting the game, story mode, or anything playable. The project says the game does not boot yet and that boot work needs an executable it does not ship.

## What it is not

- It is not an official PC version of GTA 6. Rockstar has not announced one.
- It is not a download of the game. There is no game, no key and no executable in the repository.
- It is not an emulator, and it cannot run the game from files it does not have.
- It is not a finished port. Treat any site offering a ready-made "Leonida download" as unsafe.

## Build requirements, at a high level

The repository's README lists an own Xbox Series copy, Windows 10/11 x64, about 350 GB of free work space, Python 3.12+, .NET 8, the Vulkan SDK, LLVM with the AMDGPU target, and Visual Studio 2022 with the C++ desktop workload. Those requirements describe a developer build environment, not a consumer installer.

We are not publishing a step-by-step build guide or links to game packages. If you are a developer with a lawful copy and the required toolchain, read the repository's own README and licence first.

## Why it matters

The shader translation and asset export are real engineering milestones even though nothing is playable. They show where an unofficial Xbox-to-PC recompilation effort currently stands: the static analysis and translation work is moving, while the runtime, graphics layer and missing executable remain the hard parts.

They are not evidence that GTA 6 can run on PC today. The project says so itself, and the current status table is the source to check before believing a viral clip.

## FAQ

### Can I play GTA 6 on PC through Leonida?

No. The project does not boot the game yet, and it does not include the executable.

### Does Leonida include the game files?

No. The repository says it contains no game, keys or executable. The build reads files from a copy the user provides.

### Is this an official Rockstar project?

No. It is an independent GitHub project. Rockstar has not announced a PC version.

### Should I download a "Leonida installer"?

No. The project does not distribute a ready-made build. Treat third-party installers, cracks and game packages as unsafe.

## Sources

- [ItsNotRexed/Leonida on GitHub](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida), project README and status table, checked November 23, 2026.
- [XDA Developers: GTA 6 could arrive on PC sooner than expected](https://www.xda-developers.com/gta-6-arrive-pc-soon-developer-unofficial-switch-2-zelda-ocarina-of-time-remake-port/), November 22, 2026.
- [DSOGaming: modders are trying a native PC version from the leaked Xbox build](https://www.dsogaming.com/news/modders-are-trying-to-create-a-pc-native-version-of-gta-6-with-its-leaked-xbox-series-x-build/), November 21, 2026.
- [Rockstar Games: Grand Theft Auto VI](https://www.rockstargames.com/VI), official product page.

title: Viceride GTA 6 is not a PC port: what the site actually is
excerpt: Viceride advertises a mobile cloud-gaming concept for GTA 6, not a PC port. The site shows a short demo, and there is no playable client or game download.
body:
## The short answer

Viceride is a website that advertises "GTA 6 Mobile - Android and iOS Via Cloud." It is not a PC port, it is not an official Rockstar product, and it does not provide a playable copy of the game. The site describes itself as an "independent GTA VI cloud gaming concept" and says its video playback and checkout are demos.

## What the site shows

- A 15-second prerecorded "preview" rather than a live game session.
- A device and server-region selector.
- A touch-control demo and a mock lobby conversation.
- A checkout flow that the site itself labels as a demo.

The domain was registered on November 16, 2026, and a third-party trust check by ScamAdviser currently gives it a low score. That is not proof of fraud on its own, but it is a reason to be cautious and not enter payment details or account credentials.

## Why it is not a GTA 6 PC port

A port needs the game code, a runtime and a graphics layer. Viceride's public pages show a video demo, not a running game or a downloadable client. It also does not claim to be affiliated with Rockstar. The page's own wording is "concept," which is the important word.

## What actually works today

GTA 6 is available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S. Rockstar has not announced a PC version. If you own a console, console Remote Play can stream the game to a PC screen; that is a supported way to use your PC as a display, not a PC port.

Be careful with search results that offer a "GTA 6 PC download," an APK, or a cloud client that asks for your Rockstar account. Those are the oldest malware and phishing baits around a big launch.

## What to do instead

- Use the official PlayStation or Xbox store to check platforms and availability.
- Use Remote Play from a console you own if you want the game on a PC screen.
- Do not enter payment data on a site that only shows a prerecorded demo.
- If you are researching the open-source effort, read the [Leonida project notes](/modding/leonida-gta6-pc-port).

## Sources

- [Viceride](https://viceride.com/), public site copy and demo labels, checked November 23, 2026.
- [ScamAdviser: viceride.com](https://www.scamadviser.com/check-website/viceride.com), third-party trust report, checked November 23, 2026.
- [Rockstar Games: Grand Theft Auto VI](https://www.rockstargames.com/VI), official product page.
- [Sumibako: GTA 6 on PC — no port, no emulator](https://sumibako.com/blog/gta-6-pc), November 21, 2026, for the current platform and Remote Play breakdown.

title: Tiny Skies codes (November 2026): no official codes yet
excerpt: Tiny Skies has no official Roblox codes as of November 23, 2026. Here is what the official page lists, what third-party sites are circulating, and how to redeem a code when one appears.
body:
## Current status

Checked November 23, 2026: **Tiny Skies Fighter Jet & Helicopters has no official codes.** The Roblox game description lists aircraft, modes and controls, but no code strings. Independent trackers that re-read the official page also show no active codes.

This is a "no codes yet" page, not a list of working codes. We would rather say that than send you into the game with an expired string.

## Codes you may see elsewhere

Some third-party pages list strings such as `SKYWINGS`, `JETFUEL50`, `HELIPRO`, `FLYHIGHREWARD` and `AIRACES`. We could not confirm those against the official game page or two independent trackers, so we are not marking them active. Treat any list that presents them without a check date and a source as unverified.

Do not use a code generator, an executor, or a site that asks for your Roblox password. None of those are needed to redeem a Roblox code, and they put your account at risk.

## How to redeem a code when one appears

1. Open the official **Tiny Skies Fighter Jet & Helicopters** experience on Roblox, not a copy or a private server.
2. Open the in-game menu or shop and look for a **Codes** field. The developer has not published an active code or a redemption screenshot, so the exact button may change with an update.
3. Copy the code exactly, including capital letters, and remove extra spaces.
4. Press Redeem and check your inventory or currency for the reward.

If the code fails, check the spelling first. If it still fails, the developer has likely retired it.

## What to do in the meantime

The official description lists flight school, daily rewards, missions and a hangar progression system. Those are the reliable ways to earn aircraft while no code is active.

Controls from the official game description:

- **Mouse** — fly
- **Click** — guns
- **Space** — weapons
- **R** — next weapon
- **Shift / Ctrl** — throttle
- **X** — flares
- **M** — map
- **Tab** — scores

## Sources

- [Tiny Skies Fighter Jet & Helicopters on Roblox](https://www.roblox.com/games/111410533261470/Tiny-Skies-Fighter-Jet-Helicopters), official game page and description, checked November 23, 2026.
- [BloxNew: Tiny Skies codes](https://bloxnew.com/tiny-skies-fighter-jet-and-helicopters/codes/), independent tracker, last checked November 23, 2026.
- [BloxStatus: Tiny Skies codes](https://bloxstatus.com/games/tiny-skies-fighter-jet-helicopters/codes/), independent tracker, last checked November 8, 2026.

title: Vox Seas Update 0.5 codes: confirmed, unconfirmed and expired
excerpt: Vox Seas Update 0.5 code lists disagree. Here is the one code multiple trackers list as working, the codes still being rechecked, and the ones marked expired.
body:
## Status at a glance

Checked November 23, 2026. Code trackers do not agree on the full list, so this page separates what is confirmed from what is still being rechecked and what is expired.

- **Listed as working by multiple trackers:** `175KLIKES` — 1 Stat Reset Token.
- **Reported active, but trackers are rechecking:** `THX200K` (30 minutes of double XP), `Release2026` (1 hour of double XP), `PatchReset` (1 Stat Reset Token), `Patch2Reset` (1 Stat Reset Token).
- **Disputed:** `PatchGold` (20,000 Gold). Some lists call it active; Roblox Den marks it expired.
- **Expired:** `BugFix1`, `BugFix2`, `BugFix3`, `BugFix4`, `Release`.

The official game description says the next code is tied to **200K likes**. We have not seen a newer official code posted there.

## Confirmed: 175KLIKES

`175KLIKES` grants 1 Stat Reset Token according to Roblox Den, Beebom and Game Codes Today. It was added around November 21, 2026. Redeem it soon; milestone codes are usually retired after the next one lands.

## Reported, but not consistently confirmed

These four were listed as active by Beebom and Game Codes Today, while Roblox Den marked them as "check" rather than confirmed working:

- `THX200K` — 30 minutes of double XP
- `Release2026` — 1 hour of double XP
- `PatchReset` — 1 Stat Reset Token
- `Patch2Reset` — 1 Stat Reset Token

They may still work, but we are not presenting them as guaranteed. Try them in the order above and stop if the game rejects one.

## Disputed and expired

`PatchGold` is the confusing one: Beebom listed it as active for 20,000 Gold on November 21, while Roblox Den marked it expired. Treat it as expired unless the game accepts it.

The older `BugFix1` through `BugFix4` codes and the original `Release` code are expired across the trackers we checked.

## How to redeem in Vox Seas Update 0.5

1. Launch **Vox Seas Update 0.5** on Roblox.
2. Open the menu with the three-line icon at the bottom left. On PC, `M` also opens the menu according to one tracker.
3. Open **Settings** with the gear icon.
4. Scroll to the **Codes** section.
5. Enter the code exactly, including capital letters, and press **Redeem**.

Codes are case-sensitive. If one fails, check the capitals first, then try the next code. None of the current codes is reported to require a level, group or game pass.

## What the rewards do

Double XP speeds up leveling for the listed duration. A Stat Reset Token lets you respend stat points, which is useful after a patch changes how a build works. Redeem the XP codes when you have a longer session planned rather than right before logging off.

## Sources

title: A Wasteland Full of Cats: Bethesda's Fallout-inspired cat game, explained
excerpt: Bethesda has confirmed A Wasteland Full of Cats, a Fallout-inspired hidden-object game from Devcats. Here is what is confirmed, what came from the ratings leak, and what is still unknown.
body:
## What was announced

On November 19, 2026, the official Fallout account announced **A Wasteland Full of Cats**, a Fallout-inspired adventure made with Brazilian studio **Devcats** and the animal-rescue charity **Dallas Pets Alive**. Bethesda later confirmed the project in a statement to media.

The announcement followed an Australian Classification Board listing that appeared earlier than planned. Bethesda acknowledged that some details had surfaced before the official reveal.

## What kind of game it is

Bethesda describes it as a cozy way to explore the Wasteland. Players set out to rescue Fofiño's missing friends, visit familiar locations, meet companions, and use a **Pip-Kitty** to uncover secrets and solve mysteries, one cat at a time.

The ratings listing, which is reported rather than independently confirmed by Bethesda, describes a hidden-object game with 14 locations, 33 rooms, recognizable Fallout vaults, optional puzzle levels and a final encounter with Radroaches. Treat those specifics as reported details until Bethesda shows the game.

## What is confirmed

- The game exists and is a collaboration between Bethesda, Devcats and Dallas Pets Alive.
- It is **Fallout-inspired**, not a mainline Fallout entry.
- It is a hidden-object adventure starring cats.
- Fofiño is the protagonist; the character previously appeared in Devcats' *Cats Love Boxes*.
- The project supports an animal-rescue campaign.

## What is not confirmed

There is no trailer, release date or platform list yet. Bethesda says it will share more soon. The Australian listing's room count, boss fight and level structure are reported details, not a final feature list.

It is also not **Fallout 5**. The wording "Fallout-inspired" is doing real work here: this is a smaller collaboration, not the next mainline RPG.

## Why it matters

The project is unusual for Bethesda: a charity partnership, a cozy hidden-object format, and a cat protagonist instead of a wasteland survivor. It also shows how a ratings-board leak can surface a project before the publisher is ready to announce it.

For players, the practical takeaway is simple: the game is real, the cat premise is real, and the release details are still open.

## Sources

- [Shacknews: Bethesda confirms Fallout-inspired Wasteland Full of Cats](https://www.shacknews.com/article/151446/bethesda-devcats-dallas-pets-alive-wasteland-full-of-cats), November 20, 2026.
- [PC Gamer: Bethesda confirms A Wasteland Full of Cats](https://www.pcgamer.com/games/fallout/a-new-fallout-game-has-been-rated-in-australia-and-its-a-hidden-object-game/), November 19, 2026.
- [GamesRadar+: Bethesda confirms a cat-themed Fallout-inspired adventure](https://www.gamesradar.com/games/fallout/bethesda-confirm-a-new-cat-themed-fallout-inspired-adventure-is-on-the-way-after-leaks-from-the-australian-classifications-board/), November 21, 2026.
- [Fallout on X](https://x.com/Fallout), official announcement, November 19, 2026.
